events.credibility_reason: Claim exists only as a talk abstract with no written argument found; the same authors' later talk and dissertation describe only n=3 progress or a reduction, and a 2025 survey calls the problem open.
Date and abstract known only from search summaries; the n=3 case was already settled in 1987, so this is at most a new proof of a known case.

why: The statement is a single containment for all n and all normal pairs, so restricted classes (Hermitian, n=3, essentially Hermitian, dilation class, Shitov's real-A/three-non-real-B class) are cases. Shitov 2025 is a journal-of-record case result, year 2025 so clearly after the snapshot. Drury 2004 proves only a weakened form for n=4, a changed statement, so variant. Homadi compiles known cases and Sharma proves facts about boundary matrices without claiming containment: none. The Speck dissertation abstract describes a reduction, not a proof, so none; its body is unread. The 2023 Oeding-Speck talk claims the whole conjecture but is pre-snapshot, unwritten, and contradicted in scope by the authors' later material, so doubtful rather than not_credible (established advisor, serious method, no identified error). The Jan 2024 talk is dated 23 January 2024 per snippets, three days before the snapshot. Mulero-Martinez 2026 has no read abstract; nothing establishes it settles any case, so none. No AI system appears anywhere.
doubts: The Speck dissertation body was unread; if it contains the full proof claimed in the 2023 talk, it would be an in-window unreviewed whole claim. The Mulero-Martinez 2026 paper's content is unknown and could contain a case. The Jan 2024 talk date rests on search snippets; if it were actually after 26 January it would still be a re-proof of the known n=3 case. Kovacec 1999's case attribution rests on a snippet of Shitov's introduction.
